overview: A Pacific storm brings snow to the Utah, Wyoming and Sierra mountains through Friday, then a weaker system follows over the weekend and early next week. Colder air and a cutoff low settle over the northern Rockies and Montana, while the Pacific Northwest and Sierra stay wet into the coming week.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A Pacific Northwest storm moves through Utah through early Saturday, with snow falling heaviest over the northern mountains. Snow levels drop to the northern valley floors Friday night. Dry weather returns for the weekend, then a weaker system reaches southern Utah Monday into Tuesday. Snowbasin has the top total at 23" with 12" expected Friday. Winter Storm Warnings run Thursday through Saturday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Snow is mostly confined to the higher ground here, with rain at lower elevations. Cypress Mountain sees the big totals, with the heaviest snow expected Tuesday. Whistler gets snow at times over the weekend and Monday, then a mix of snow and rain as the week goes on.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A cold system brings snow to the Tetons and the mountain passes Thursday night through Friday, with Teton Pass likely to have travel problems. Jackson Hole and Grand Targhee see the most snow Friday. A Winter Weather Advisory covers Thursday night through Friday night. Colder air arrives across Montana over the weekend, with snow showers around West Yellowstone and Southwest Montana into Saturday and dry weather after that.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A strong storm brings heavy snow to the Sierra and southern Cascades, with strong winds on the ridges. Snow tapers Friday, then a weaker system arrives Saturday night into Monday. Palisades and Sugar Bowl each expect around 8" on Sunday. Winter Storm Warnings for Palisades and Sugar Bowl run through Friday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: The Pacific Northwest stays dry Friday under fog and high pressure. Rain and mountain snow arrive Saturday night as a weak low sits offshore, with light totals. Crystal Mountain gets snow Saturday through Tuesday, with its biggest day expected Tuesday. Heavier precipitation returns mid-week.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Snow showers run through the Colorado mountains Thursday night into Saturday, with blowing snow and gusts up to 45 mph Friday. The main system is convective and banded, so totals are uncertain. Aspen Highlands and Telluride see the best chances Friday and Saturday. Cold air settles in over the weekend.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Strong winds hit the southern Sangres and I-25 gaps Friday, with a High Wind Warning. A quick system brings snow to the mountains Friday night, then another light round Saturday. Wolf Creek sees blowing snow through Friday night. Taos gets snow showers Saturday. A cold, unsettled pattern continues into next week.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
